case3.conclusion: The registered open two-face crack fixture fails: negative-gradient displacement lowers this loss while increasing the shared-endpoint gap. The recorded finite difference supports the gradient implementation.
case3.limitation: The two-triangle patch has a physical open outer boundary. This tests the complete localized boundary current, including that outer boundary; it is not an isolated crack-only energy or proof that every closed-mesh crack is repelled. The gate still fails as registered.

case4_same_GT_normals.conclusion: Restoring both faces to the same trusted direction prevents the odd-input-winding cancellation and gives four times the single-triangle energy, within recorded FP64 rounding.

case4_opposite_GT_normals.conclusion: A fundamental non-identifiability of this oriented-current objective: coincident nondegenerate faces with opposite trusted reference orientations have opposite directed edge vectors and identical midpoint kernels, so their contributions cancel at every probe and scale. Trusted-normal sign correction cannot remove this counterexample.
case4_opposite_GT_normals.evidence_scope: The saved finite-probe CPU result supports the analytic cancellation; no further loss or gradient evaluation was performed.

case4_nearby_parallel_faces.conclusion: The recorded separation directional derivative is positive; gradient descent reduces the small separation, supporting attraction toward the cancellation configuration in this fixture.

oracle_orientation.conclusion: The separately saved source-ID and winding audit supports the raw/restored GT oracle orientation. The archive-naive orientation is inconsistent and is retained as a diagnostic. Small oracle loss alone would not establish correctness, as case4b demonstrates.
oracle_orientation.limits: Two-face opposite edge directions do not by themselves establish outward normals, absence of embedded intersections, or vertex manifoldness. Raw/restored source-normal supervision is not an inference input.
